what: The SIP Calculator estimates how much a regular monthly investment could be worth after a number of years at an expected yearly return. It also has a lump sum mode for a single investment.
You can add a yearly step-up, which raises your monthly amount by a percentage every year. A chart compares what you invest with the estimated value, and a table shows every year.
The results are estimates based on a steady average return. Real markets rise and fall, so treat the numbers as a guide, not a guarantee.
uses: See how a monthly amount could grow over 20 or 30 years.
Try different amounts to see what you need for a future goal.
Compare a flat monthly amount with one that grows 10% a year.
Check what a bonus invested once could become.
Show how gains grow faster than deposits over time.
tutorial: Tap Monthly investment (SIP) for regular investing or Lump sum for a single amount.
Choose from the list or type your own symbol.
Type the monthly investment, or the one-time amount in lump sum mode.
Type a yearly return, for example 10 for 10%. Use a cautious figure; long-term averages for diversified funds are often lower than recent years.
Type the number of years (up to 100). In SIP mode, add a yearly step-up percentage if you plan to invest more each year.
See how much you invest, the estimated gains and the total value. Tap the chart to see any year, and scroll the table for details.
features: Raise the monthly amount by a percentage every year.
Invested amount and estimated value side by side.
Monthly amount, total invested, gains and value for each year.
Monthly compounding with payments at the start of each month, like most SIP calculators.
Share the result in one tap.

example.title: Worked example: 1,000 a month for 10 years at 12%
example.text: You invest 1,000 at the start of every month for 120 months, a total of 120,000. With a 12% yearly return (1% a month), the estimated value is about 232,339, so the gains are about 112,339. Adding a 10% yearly step-up raises the total invested to about 191,249 and the value to about 337,433.

tips: Start early: time in the market does more than a slightly higher amount.
A small step-up each year keeps your investing in line with a growing salary.
Use a lower return to allow for fees, tax and inflation.
Compare with the Inflation Calculator to see what the future value is worth in today’s money.
problems: The amount and years must be above 0, the return between −99 and 100%, and the step-up from 0 to 100%.
My fund app shows a different value
Apps use real prices and dates. This tool assumes a steady return, so results will differ.
The chart has only two points
The period is under a year. Use a longer period to see a curve.
